Bundi , under Section 7 read with Section 16 of Prevention of Food
Adulteration Act, 1954, be dropped inter alia on the following
grounds:-

( a) That in the present case, complaint was filed after period of three years, hence, the same is barred under Section 468 Cr.P.C.
(b) That in the present case, trial is being conducted by Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Bundi, and he is not competent court to Raju @ Rajendra Kumar S/O Shri Gordhan ... vs State Of Rajasthan on 6 February, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175959443/

] 
try the offence as per Section 16(A) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.
(c) That as per the notification issued by State Government after enactment of the Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006 proceedings are to be dropped against the petitioner.
I find no merit in all the three arguments raised by counsel for the petitioner.
Briefly stated that the Food Inspector on 09.08.2001 took into possession the sample of chilli powder from the shop of the petitioner.
The said sample were sent to the food laboratory and same was found adulterated.

Legislature by an amendment has specifically held that Section 468 Cr.P.C.
will not apply qua the socio-economic offences.
To sell the adulterated food is a socio- economic offence, therefore, Section 468 is not applicable.
Reference can be made to the Economic Offences(inapplicability of Limitation Act, 1974) to reject the argument raised by counsel for the petitioner.

So far, second argument is concerned court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bundi, indeed is a court of Judicial Magistrate whereas Section 16-A only apply to the cases which are to be tried summarily.
In the present case, petitioner is not being tried summarily.

So far third argument is concerned a perusal of the notification issued by the State Government reveal that it has been stated therein that only those offences which are not serious after enactment of Food Safety and Standard Act 2006 are not be tried.
To sell the adulterated food is a serious offence as it causes havoc in the society.

] Consequently, having rejected the three arguments raised by counsel for the petitioner, I find no merit in the present petition and the same is dismissed.
(KANWALJIT SINGH AHLUWALIA),J Heena/223
